answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using hardware enclave attestation. Agents generate proofs rooted in physical silicon, forcing adversaries to incur the verifiable cost of distinct processor dies per identity instead of branching across a virtualized vine. Registries reject any vulnerable relic chip and verify firmware via a cedar root authority. However, this mechanism relies on trusted chip fabricators and remains vulnerable to microarchitectural side-channel leaks.
